polynomial.title: What is a Polynomial Function?
polynomial.intro: A polynomial function is a function made up of terms that are variables raised to whole number powers, multiplied by coefficients.
polynomial.discovery: Let's explore the beautiful world of polynomials! From modeling population growth to designing roller coasters, these versatile functions power modern technology and science.

operations.title: Operations with Polynomials
operations.intro: Just like numbers, polynomials can be added, subtracted, multiplied, and divided. The key is organizing terms by their degree!

anatomy.title: Anatomy of a Polynomial
anatomy.caption: Each term has a coefficient, variable, and exponent (degree)

multiplying.title: Multiplying Polynomials
multiplying.caption: Distribute each term to every term in the other polynomial

degree.title: Polynomial Degree Determines Its Name:
degree.content: The degree is the highest exponent in the polynomial.

example1.step3: Step 3: Combine like terms by degree

example3.title: Example 3: Evaluating a Polynomial
example3.problem: If f(x) = 2x³ - 3x² + 1, find f(0) and explain what it represents.
example3.answer: f(0) = 1, which is the y-intercept (where the graph crosses the y-axis)

mistake1.title: Confusing Degree with Number of Terms
mistake1.wrong: Students think x³ has degree 3 because "it has 3 in the exponent and must have 3 terms":
mistake1.correct: Degree is the highest exponent, NOT the number of terms:
mistake1.explanation: A polynomial's degree tells you the highest power of x, not how many terms it has. x³ is a single term with degree 3. Meanwhile, x + x² + 1 has 3 terms but degree 2!
mistake1.tip: Count terms by counting the + and - signs (plus one). Count degree by finding the biggest exponent.

mistake2.title: FOIL Errors When Multiplying
mistake2.wrong: When multiplying (x + 2)(x - 3), students forget the middle terms:
mistake2.correct: Use FOIL (First, Outer, Inner, Last) for ALL four products:
mistake2.explanation: You must multiply EVERY term in the first binomial by EVERY term in the second. That's 2 × 2 = 4 products. Missing any term gives the wrong answer!

mistake3.title: Adding Exponents Instead of Coefficients
mistake3.wrong: When simplifying x²(x + 3), students might write x² + 3x:
mistake3.correct: When multiplying, ADD exponents; when adding, combine coefficients:
mistake3.explanation: x² · x = x³ (exponents add: 2 + 1 = 3). But x² + x cannot be simplified further because they're not like terms!

realWorld.title: Real-World Applications
realWorld.intro: Polynomial functions model countless real-world phenomena—from economics to physics to computer graphics!

app1.title: 📈 Population Modeling
app1.description: Scientists use polynomial functions to model population growth over time.
app1.example: A city's population might be P(t) = 0.01t³ - 0.5t² + 10t + 50000, where t is years since 2000

app2.title: 💼 Economics & Cost Analysis
app2.description: Businesses use polynomials to model costs, revenue, and profit.
app2.example: Total cost might be C(x) = 0.002x³ - 0.5x² + 50x + 1000, where x is units produced

app3.title: 🎮 Computer Graphics
app3.description: Polynomial curves (Bezier curves) create smooth shapes in animation and design.
app3.example: Video game characters, font designs, and 3D models all use polynomial curves for smooth motion

exercise1.question: What is the degree of 4x³ - 2x² + 7x - 5?
exercise1.explanation: The degree is the highest exponent, which is 3 (from the x³ term)

exercise2.question: How many terms does 3x⁴ - 2x² + 2x² + x - 7 have before combining like terms? Enter the number.
exercise2.hint: Count each separate piece before simplifying.
exercise2.explanation: Before combining: 3x⁴, -2x², +2x², x, -7. That's 5 terms. (After combining the x² terms, it becomes 3 terms)

exercise3.question: Simplify: (3x² - x + 1) + (-x² + 2x + 1). What is the result?

exercise4.question: If f(x) = x³ - 2x + 6, what is f(2)? Enter the number.

exercise5.question: Which polynomial has a y-intercept of -3?
exercise5.explanation: The y-intercept occurs when x = 0. All three functions equal -3 when x = 0, so the answer is 'All of the above'!

exercise6.question: A box has volume V(x) = x³ - 6x² + 9x. For what positive value of x is the volume zero? Enter the number.
exercise6.hint: Factor out x first, then factor the remaining quadratic.
exercise6.explanation: V(x) = x(x² - 6x + 9) = x(x - 3)². Solutions: x = 0 or x = 3. The positive value is 3.

notes.title: Tips & Strategies
notes.tip1: 📝 Always organize polynomials in descending order by degree (highest power first). This makes operations much easier!
notes.tip2: 🎯 When adding or subtracting, ONLY combine like terms (same variable, same exponent). 3x² and 5x are NOT like terms!
notes.tip3: 💡 The degree of the product when multiplying is the SUM of the degrees. (Degree 2) × (Degree 3) = Degree 5 polynomial!

conclusion.title: You're Now a Polynomial Pro! 🎉
conclusion.summary: Polynomial functions are among the most versatile tools in mathematics. From modeling real-world data to computer graphics, you'll use these skills throughout your STEM journey!
conclusion.takeaway1: Polynomial degree is the highest exponent in the expression
conclusion.takeaway2: Add/subtract polynomials by combining like terms
conclusion.takeaway3: Multiply polynomials by distributing each term to all other terms
conclusion.takeaway4: The number of terms doesn't equal the degree!
